Q: constexpr always good ? in C++ A:

No. There are always tradeoffs to everything, even if as simple as "if you want to compile quickly, definitely don't go for a lot of difficult compile-time calculations".

Compile-time evaluation usually does improve runtime and reliability, but it's not necessarily to a perceptible extent so don't overfocus on it - constexpr isn't a magic bullet that'll fix all your problems. It matters sometimes and you still need to know when it matters.

Q: How to make my Timer fire in Release Build? A:

Since the behavior changes with -fno-inline and OptimizeCode = Never, this looks less like a timer issue and more like an optimization/ODR or ABI mismatch across the library and Unreal module boundary. I’d compare the exact compiler, visibility/LTO settings, Boost/Asio-related defines, and preprocessor flags between the dependency build and the UE module.
